text:
alex: Heads-up: acme-inc started getting 429s from our dedicated pool ~09:20 UTC. Customer says it began right after their plan migration. They see lots of small, consistent spikes rather than one big burst.

maya: Can you paste an example 429 response body / headers? Want to check which limiter fired (global vs per-tenant).

alex: Here's one response from their app logs (sanitized):

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 3600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "detail": "tenant quota exceeded (window: hour)"
}
```

maya: X-RateLimit-Limit = 3600 window=hour looks like a per-hour ceiling. acme expected a per-minute config.

jordan: I pulled the tenant quota object from the admin store for acme-inc. Looks like the migration script applied a unit field of "hour" instead of "minute" during the plan migration. Effective allowance = configured_value * (unit multiplier). In this case acme was supposed to get 600 requests/min (36k/hour) but the stored record is 600/hour -> 60x lower. That explains widespread 429s despite free GPU headroom.

ops-oncall: Verified dedicated pool utilization: GPUs at ~40% and autoscale had room to add more replicas, so this is clearly limiter-side, not infra saturation or noisy neighbor eviction. Logs show per-tenant token-bucket hits: 

```
[2026-03-12T09:21:34Z] limiter=tenant-bucket tenant=acme-inc allowed=600 window=hour used=600 overflow=true
[2026-03-12T09:21:58Z] handler=req id=... status=429 reason=tenant_quota_exceeded
```

maya: Repro steps for ops/eng to validate locally:
1) Query admin API: 
   curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>' https://admin.internal/api/tenants/acme-inc/quota
   Expect to see unit: "hour" and value: 600 (wrong)
2) Simulate steady traffic: run a loop of 10 reqs/sec for 2 minutes from one host and watch X-RateLimit-Remaining drop to 0 quickly.

jordan: Immediate mitigation options:
- apply a temporary override to the tenant quota with the admin API to correct unit to "minute" (or multiply value by 60)
- rollback the migration change if it's gated and affects many tenants
- create a short-lived per-tenant exception allowing higher burst while we fix the data layer

Suggested patch (one-off):
```bash
curl -X PATCH -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_TOKEN>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  'https://admin.internal/api/tenants/acme-inc/quota' \
  -d '{"rate_value": 36000, "rate_unit": "hour", "note": "temp fix: converted from per-minute to per-hour"}'
```

ops-oncall: I'll apply the override now and monitor. Will also add a short rule in routing to prefer fallback model variants if we see repeated 429s.

support-bot: Customer reported: "sudden rate limit errors after plan change — impacting search UX". Ticket #INC-2026-487 created and linked to this thread.

jordan: Post-mortem action items:
- roll back or fix the migration script to preserve unit semantics (minute vs hour) and add unit tests that assert no unit drift
- run a one-off audit: list tenants with mismatched unit/value ratios vs plan expectations and enqueue fixes
- add monitoring alert for when a tenant sees >30% 429s in a 5m window while pool utilization <70%

maya: Thanks. ops-oncall, can you paste the exact admin API response you saw after the override so we can confirm?

ops-oncall: Override applied at 09:26 UTC. New admin GET shows: 
```
{
  "tenant": "acme-inc",
  "rate_value": 36000,
  "rate_unit": "hour",
  "effective_description": "converted from 600/min -> 36000/hour (temp)"
}
```

alex: Customer verified errors stopped after ~2 min of traffic following the patch. They've been notified and asked for RCA.

jordan: I'll open a PR to change the migration and backfill script, include the audit query, and assign to release for hotfix. Also scheduling a retro with product to review plan-migration process.

alex: Closing loop here — ticket updated with mitigation and timeline. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
